description: Test cases for shell-script-reviewer. Each case's script should be written to a temp file with the given extension and reviewed per SKILL.md. expected_findings defines the minimum bar for recall (every listed finding must be surfaced, at >= the given severity); must_not_exceed_severity is a precision check for the clean cases; must_not_mention is a policy check -- e.g. verifying the reviewer never recommends adding set -e/set -u, since this skill treats their presence as a finding rather than their absence.

expected_findings.reason: $files is unquoted in rm -rf $files; a value like '* --no-preserve-root' or multiple space-separated paths expands to unintended targets

cases.focus: unchecked critical commands -- no set -e present, and none should be recommended
cases.script:
#!/bin/bash
BUILD_DIR=build
cd $BUILD_DIR
rm -rf ./*
mkdir artifacts
cp ../dist/* artifacts/
echo "done"

expected_findings.reason: cd $BUILD_DIR has no failure check; if it fails, rm -rf ./* runs in the original directory
mkdir and cp have no explicit exit-status checks; a failure in either is silently ignored and the script reports 'done' regardless

cases.note: the fix here is explicit per-command checks, not adding a strict-mode header -- this skill flags -e/-u as an anti-pattern, so the review must not recommend adding them

expected_findings.reason: eval "run_$step" executes attacker-controlled shell code if $step contains shell metacharacters (e.g. 'build; rm -rf /')

cases.script:
#!/bin/bash
set -o pipefail
Dir="$1"
Count=`ls "$Dir" | wc -l`
if [ "$Count" -gt 0 ]
then
	echo "Found $Count files"
fi

expected_findings.reason: backticks instead of $(...), PascalCase variable names instead of lowercase_with_underscores, then/do not on the same line as if

cases.note: quoting is already correct and only pipefail (this skill's recommended baseline, no -e/-u) is present, so nothing here should be scored Critical or High

cases.focus: set -euo pipefail present with no explicit checks -- should itself be flagged under this skill's policy
cases.script:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
input_dir="$1"
output_dir="$2"
mkdir -p "$output_dir"
cp "$input_dir"/*.log "$output_dir"/
echo "copied logs"

expected_findings.reason: set -euo pipefail is present with no explicit per-command checks of its own; per this skill's convention, -e/-u should be removed in favor of explicit `cmd || exit` checks -- set -o pipefail alone is fine to keep

cases.note: everything else in this script is already correct (quoting, no destructive unguarded glob, no eval) -- this case exists specifically to verify the reviewer flags -e/-u presence itself rather than treating it as a good practice

cases.focus: unquoted expansion injection risk that survives zsh's word-splitting defaults
cases.script:
#!/usr/bin/env zsh
targets=("$@")
for t in ${targets[@]}; do
  rsync -a $t /backup/
done

expected_findings.reason: array expansions and $t are unquoted; array-element splitting still applies in zsh regardless of SH_WORD_SPLIT, and a path with a leading '-' could be parsed as an rsync flag

cases.focus: no explicit error handling on critical commands -- setopt ERR_EXIT/NO_UNSET should not be the recommended fix

expected_findings.reason: cd $deploy_dir has no explicit failure check; if it fails, ./release.sh still runs from the original directory

cases.note: the fix is an explicit cd || exit check, not a setopt ERR_EXIT/NO_UNSET header -- this skill flags those as an anti-pattern

expected_findings.reason: $filter is interpolated into a string passed to eval; a value like ''' -o -exec rm -rf {} ; ''' breaks out of the intended find invocation

cases.focus: stylistically non-compliant but functionally correct, includes a 0-index assumption note
cases.script:
#!/usr/bin/env zsh
setopt PIPE_FAIL
arr=(alpha beta gamma)
first=$arr[1]
echo "first element: $first"

expected_findings.reason: correct 1-indexed usage for zsh but unquoted $arr[1] access and no comment noting the indexing differs from bash for readers porting code

cases.note: arr[1] correctly returns 'alpha' in zsh (1-indexed) -- reviewer must not flag this as an off-by-one bug. Only PIPE_FAIL is set (no ERR_EXIT/NO_UNSET), matching this skill's recommended baseline, so that should not be flagged either

cases.focus: unquoted expansion used to build a destructive command

expected_findings.reason: no validation that $argv[1] was actually provided; an empty $target makes rm -rf $target/* equivalent to rm -rf /*

cases.focus: missing $status checks -- fish has no errexit equivalent
cases.script:
#!/usr/bin/env fish
mkdir /tmp/build
cd /tmp/build
tar xf archive.tar.gz
./configure
make

expected_findings.reason: no $status checks or and/or chaining after mkdir/cd/tar; fish has no set -e equivalent so failures are silently ignored and later commands run in the wrong state
fish's eval builtin executes $cmd as shell code; passing it directly from argv is arbitrary command execution

cases.script:
#!/usr/bin/env fish
function GetCount
set f $argv[1]
set c (cat $f | wc -l | string trim)
echo $c
end
GetCount data.txt

expected_findings.reason: PascalCase function name instead of snake_case, no indentation inside the function body, and shells out to cat/wc where fish's own tooling (or wc alone via redirection) would suffice

cases.note: cat $f | wc -l works correctly here; this is a style-only finding, not a correctness bug
